office: the Registrar-General for the Registration of Persons
note: The Registration of Persons Act 1989 (7 MIRC Ch. 16, consolidated, on the Nitijela's site; read 2026-11-03): every citizen may apply for registration regardless of age (§1606(1)), and the Registrar-General issues an identity card as soon as practicable after registration (§1613(1)); the fee is an amount the Registrar-General determines (§1621), which wasn't found, so it's null; the Act sets no term and no time. Until then the entry stood on the SEAP digital ID overview, which says the same of who may hold it.

sources.title: Nitijela of the Republic of the Marshall Islands: Registration of Persons Act 1989 (7 MIRC Ch.16), consolidated
sources.said: §1606. (1) Every person who is a citizen of the Republic and who is not eligible to register under Subsection (2) of this Section shall be eligible to apply for registration, regardless of that persons age. ... §1613. (1) The Registrar-General shall, as soon as practicable after a person is registered issue to that person an identity card. ... §1621. Fees. A fee in an amount to be determined by the Registrar-General shall be paid with each application to cover any administrative or other expenses necessary for the implementation of this Chapter.
